items.definition:
magnificent and splendid appearance; grandeur
The palace was decorated with great splendor.

a distinct component of a larger structure
The protein is composed of several smaller subunits.

a judgment that a person is not guilty of the crime with which they have been charged
The jury's acquittal brought relief to the defendant.

military weapons and equipment
The country was increasing its armament in response to regional tensions.

a secret political clique or faction
A small cabal of conspirators planned the overthrow of the government.

a small group of people specially trained for a particular purpose or profession
The party relied on a dedicated cadre of activists.

the invention of a new word or phrase; coins collectively
The term "cyberspace" was a new coinage in the 1980s.

the process of deriving something; origin
The derivation of the word "robot" is from Czech.

the effort to match or surpass a person or achievement
His work was worthy of emulation by his peers.

an advocate of a federal system of government
The Federalists supported a strong central government.

a sudden attack or a brief venture
Her first foray into entrepreneurship was a small online store.

the loss or giving up of something
The contract stipulated forfeiture of the deposit if the terms were not met.

unverified information heard from others
The lawyer argued that the evidence was merely hearsay and inadmissible.

a wealthy and influential person, especially in business
The shipping magnate owned a fleet of cargo ships.

a funeral home or morgue
The body was taken to the mortuary.

a doctor specializing in the nervous system
She consulted a neurologist about her headaches.

a military officer responsible for supplies
The quartermaster ensured the troops had enough provisions.

the practice of exchanging things with others for mutual benefit
The agreement was based on the principle of reciprocity.

the quality of reacting quickly and positively
The company is known for its excellent customer responsiveness.

sanctity (the state or quality of being holy, sacred, or saintly)
The sanctity of human life is a fundamental principle in many cultures.

sedition (conduct or speech inciting people to rebel against the authority of a state or monarch)
The journalist was accused of sedition for publishing articles critical of the government.

stave (a vertical wooden plank forming part of the side of a barrel or similar container; a set of five parallel lines on which musical notes are written)
The old barrel was missing a few staves, making it unusable.

swami (a Hindu male religious teacher)
The swami shared ancient wisdom with his disciples.

a collection of valuable items
The archaeologists discovered a trove of ancient artifacts.

a winding device used for pulling or lifting
They used a winch to pull the boat onto the trailer.

the market for spare parts, accessories, and services for products
The company specializes in aftermarket car parts.

a secret love affair
The novel described a passionate amour between the two characters.

official agreement or approval
The committee gave its assent to the new proposal.

the middle class
The novel satirized the values of the bourgeoisie.

a negative electrode
Electrons flow from the anode to the cathode.

involvement in a crime or wrongdoing
He denied any complicity in the fraud.

the spread of disease or influence
The financial crisis led to economic contagion across the globe.

a stress hormone
Stress can lead to elevated levels of cortisol in the body.

a state of complete emptiness or destruction; great unhappiness
The abandoned town was a scene of utter desolation.

a comprehensive listing of musical recordings
The band's discography includes ten studio albums.

a type of fish, also known as mahi-mahi
We ordered grilled dorado at the seafood restaurant.

a person who is not Jewish
In some religious contexts, a gentile refers to a non-Jew.

the process of renovating and improving a house or district so that it conforms to middle-class taste
Gentrification often leads to rising property values and displacement of original residents.

A particular point in events or time.
At this critical juncture, we must make a decision.

a change of the form or nature of a thing or person into a completely different one
The caterpillar undergoes a complete metamorphosis into a butterfly.

The process by which green plants and some other organisms use sunlight to synthesize foods.
Plants use photosynthesis to convert light into energy.

The tip of a dancer's toe, especially in ballet.
Ballerinas often dance en pointe.

A monastery governed by a prior or prioress.
The old priory stood on a hill overlooking the village.

The action of remedying something, especially the reversal or stopping of damage.
The school offered remediation classes for struggling students.

A musical form in which a main theme returns several times in alternation with other themes.
The final movement of the symphony was a lively rondo.

A sailing ship with two or more masts, typically with fore-and-aft sails.
The old schooner sailed gracefully across the bay.

The principle of separation of the state from religious institutions.
Secularism advocates for a society free from religious rule.

The state of being a slave or completely subject to someone more powerful.
The country abolished all forms of servitude.

the undermining of power or authority
The government accused the group of subversion.

hard and continuous work
After years of toil, he finally achieved his dream.

the quality or state of being uniform
The company strives for uniformity in its product quality.

strength, energy, or enthusiasm
He tackled the project with renewed vigor.

the explosive part of a missile or bomb
The missile carried a powerful warhead.

an evergreen tree or shrub
The ancient yew tree stood tall in the churchyard.

a person from former Yugoslavia
Many Yugoslav immigrants settled in Germany.

a gelatinous substance used in cooking and science
Agar is often used as a vegetarian gelling agent.

a person who believes that nothing is known or can be known of the existence or nature of God
He identifies as an agnostic, neither believing nor disbelieving in God.

the surgical removal of a limb or body part
The doctor performed an amputation to save the patient's life.

The process of breaking into small parts or fragments.
The old building was in a state of complete disintegration.

Lack of harmony or agreement.
There was a noticeable dissonance between his words and his actions.

Threats, violence, constraints, or other action used to coerce someone into doing something against their will or better judgment.
He claimed he signed the contract under duress.

Theft or misappropriation of funds placed in one's trust or belonging to one's employer.
She was charged with embezzlement of company funds.

literature or art dealing with sexual love in an explicit or stimulating way
The bookstore had a section dedicated to erotica.

the action of exciting someone or something, or the state of being excited
The excitation of the atoms caused them to emit light.
